_note: Open legal and privacy points, one row each. Written by the weekly compliance review (BRIEF_COMPLIANCE.md) and by sessions; read by scripts/quality.py's compliance_cell (orange while a row is open). owner: hidde (a decision only he can make) or session (work a session can do). Never delete a row: set status fixed (with fixed_in), declined (with his words) or not_needed (with why).

findings.summary: On 2026-10-29 the 33 accounts that had chosen a private profile were made public without asking them.
findings.law: GDPR art. 25(2) privacy by default; art. 6 lawful basis
findings.fix: Set those 33 back to private, or mail them once with the choice and keep private for whoever does not answer.
findings.why: Hidde, 2026-11-10, shown the four with options: "dit risico accepteer ik negeer dit vanaf nu"

findings.summary: New accounts get a public profile (name, picture, Collected, Want to go) visible to anybody signed in, without a choice at sign-up.
findings.law: GDPR art. 25(2): data not made accessible to an indefinite number of people without the person's intervention
findings.fix: One clear choice when the account is made (public or private), or at least a visible notice with the switch at sign-up.
findings.why: Hidde, 2026-11-10, shown the four with options: "dit risico accepteer ik negeer dit vanaf nu"

findings.summary: The privacy page names only 'Ancient Trees, a small independent project in the Netherlands' and info@: no person and no business registration. His rule 'zet mijn naam er nooit onder' (2026-08-24, qa check_no_owner_name) refuses his name on every page but /about, so the legal identity GDPR asks for is not on the page.
findings.law: GDPR art. 13(1)(a) identity of the controller; Dutch Civil Code 3:15d once there is economic activity
findings.fix: Either a KvK registration whose trade name and number go on the privacy page, or his yes to his full name on /privacy only (widen check_no_owner_name for that page).
findings.why: Hidde, 2026-11-10, shown the four with options: "dit risico accepteer ik negeer dit vanaf nu"

findings.summary: The app sends PostHog an install id and, signed in, the account number, without asking first; no retention is set or stated.
findings.law: Telecommunicatiewet 11.7a (device storage needs consent unless strictly necessary); GDPR art. 13(2)(a)
findings.fix: Ask in the app before analytics starts, or drop the account number and keep only anonymous counts; set a retention in PostHog and name it on the privacy page.
findings.why: Hidde, 2026-11-10, shown the four with options: "dit risico accepteer ik negeer dit vanaf nu"

findings.summary: A photograph somebody mails us goes on the site at once and the reply asks afterwards whether that is ok (rule of 2026-10-14).
findings.law: Auteurswet art. 1 and 12: publishing needs the maker's permission
findings.fix: Ask in the first reply and publish on the yes; or treat 'here are photos for your site' as the yes and record those words with the photo.

findings.summary: Sentences from people's mails (data/outreach-words.json) are quoted on tree pages without asking them; mails fall outside the app's terms.
findings.fix: One line in the reply: 'May we put this sentence on the tree's page, without your name?', and quote on the yes.

findings.summary: The website now links the licence and the source of every CC photograph; the app still prints the name and licence as plain text.
findings.law: CC BY / BY-SA section 3(a): licence URI and source where reasonably practicable
findings.fix: Send licence_url and source_url in the feed (lib/images.ts licenceUrl and photoSourceUrl) and make the app's credit line tappable.
